== History ==
The shrine serves as an external shrine of the {{ill|Sayū Shrine|ja|左右神社|qid=Q59282615}}, overseen by the Kamishiro family. The enshrined deities are {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|az|Konohanasakuya|ca|Konohana no Sakuya hime|de|Konohanasakuyahime|fa|کونوهاناساکویا-هیمه|fr|Konohana-no-Sakuya|it|Konohanasakuya-hime|ja|コノハナノサクヤビメ|ko|고노하나노사쿠야비메|mni|ꯀꯣꯅꯣꯍꯅꯁꯀꯨꯌ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Konohanasakuya-hime|ru|Коноханасакуя-химэ|sv|Konohanasakuyahime|th|เซ็นเง็ง|vi|Konohana Sakuya Hime|zh|木花開耶姬|qid=Q1781862}} (Konoha-no-sakuya-hime-no-mikoto), {{ill|Izanagi|abstract|Q813858|ar|إزاناغي|az|İzanaqi|bcl|Izanagi|bn|ইজানাগি|bs|Izanagi|ca|Izanagi|cs|Izanagi a Izanami|da|Izanagi|el|Ιζανάγκι|eo|Izanagi|es|Izanagi|fa|ایزاناگی|fi|Izanaki|fr|Izanagi|he|איזאנגי|hr|Izanagi|hu|Izanagi|id|Izanagi|it|Izanagi|ja|イザナギ|ka|იძანაგი|ko|이자나기|lt|Idzanagis|mk|Изанаги|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯒꯤ|no|Izanagi|or|ଇଜାନାଗି|pt|Izanagi|ro|Izanagi|rsk|Изанаґи|ru|Идзанаги|simple|Izanagi|sk|Izanagi|sl|Izanagi|sr|Изанаки|sv|Izanagi|ta|இசநாகி|th|อิซานางิ|tl|Izanagi|tr|İzanagi|uk|Ідзанаґі|vi|Izanagi|zh|伊邪那岐|qid=Q813858}} (Izanagi-no-mikoto), and {{ill|Izanami|ar|إزانامي|az|İzanami|bcl|Izanami|bs|Izanami|ca|Izanami|da|Izanami|el|Ιζανάμι|eo|Izanami|es|Izanami|fa|ایزانامی|fi|Izanami|fr|Izanami|he|איזאנמי|hr|Izanami|hu|Izanami|hy|Իզանամի|id|Izanami|it|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|ko|이자나미|mk|Изанами|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯃꯤ|pt|Izanami|rsk|Изанами|ru|Идзанами|simple|Izanami|sl|Izanami|sr|Изанами|sv|Izanami|ta|இசநமி|th|อิซานามิ|tl|Izanami|tr|Izanami|uk|Ідзанамі|zh|伊邪那美|qid=Q682306}} (Izanami-no-mikoto).

The exact date of its establishment is unknown, but it has been worshiped in this area since ancient times. Historically, the shrine has been revered as "Koyasu-sama of Sakurai" due to its blessings for good relationships, childbirth, and fertility. It was also known as "Sakurai Koyasu Daijin" in the past.

According to oral tradition, the shrine's red hemp cord (Koyasu-sama's red belt) symbolizes connections not only between couples but also between parents and children. It is believed that carrying the cord can fulfill wishes related to good relationships and fertility. Over time, it has also become a charm for health, academic success, and good fortune.

In addition, as some households in the region perform {{ill|Shinto funeral|ja|神葬祭|qid=Q11590783}} (Shinto-style funerals), the shrine is respected as a guardian deity overseeing the entire life cycle—from birth, through rites of passage like {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ar|شيشي قو سان|ca|Shichi-Go-San|da|Shichi-go-san|de|Shichi-go-san|es|Shichi-Go-San|fa|شیچی-گو-سان|fi|Shichi-go-san|fr|Shichi-go-san|hu|Sicsi-Go-Szan|hy|Սիչի-Գո-Սան|id|Shichi-Go-San|it|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三|ko|시치고산|lt|Šičigosan|mn|Шичигосан|ms|Shichi-Go-San|my|ရှိချိဂေါ့ဆန်း|nl|Shichi-Go-San|pl|Shichi-go-san|pt|Shichi-Go-San|ru|Сити-го-сан|simple|Shichi-Go-San|sv|Shichi-go-san|tr|Shichi-Go-San|vi|Shichi-Go-San|zh|七五三|qid=Q1072387|lt=Shichi-Go-San}}, to funerals.

* January 1 - Saitan-sai (New Year's Festival)
* September - Ujigami Festival
* November - Annual Festival
* 1st and 15th of every month - Tsukinami-sai (Monthly Festival)

== Access ==
From JR Sōbu Main Line, get off at Asahi Station, then walk 11 minutes from the Banzai Elementary School bus stop.
